newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May gasoline output hit 8.14 mln bpd high-API.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May gasoline output hit 8.14 mln bpd high-API.

text.p: U.S. gasoline production and petroleum imports surged to new highs in May, feeding a rapidly growing domestic appetite for oil, according to an American Petroleum Institute report released Wednesday.

Refineries in May pumped out a record 8.04 million barrels per day of gasoline, up 4.0 percent from a year ago, while refineries used 15.11 million bpd of crude, the highest volume since December 1979 and 4.2 percent more than a year ago, API said in its monthly report.
Total U.S. petroleum demand jumped 2.6 percent from May 1996 to 18.33 million bpd, "reflecting robust economic growth and lower product prices," it said.

To help fill the demand and build depleted stocks, imports of crude oil and products in May rose 3.1 percent from a year ago to 10.23 million bpd, beating the previous record of 10.14 million bpd in April.
Products imports accounted for most of the leap, soaring 15 percent to 2.17 million bpd. Crude oil imports were almost unchanged at 8.06 million bpd.
API said more than 1 million bpd of the petroleum imports went into inventories "in one of the largest single-month stock builds in six years."

If refiners had drawn down their stocks at the same rate as they had last year, imports through the first five months of this year would have climbed by only 1 percent instead of 7.3 percent, it said.
Crude stocks at the end of May were at 324 million barrels, 19 million barrels higher than a year ago, and the highest level since June 1995.
However, stocks of gasoline and blending components at the end of May at 201 million barrels stood 4 million barrels below May 1996 levels and 14 million barrels below a recent-year average.
U.S. crude production was roughly unchanged from a year ago at 6.4 million bpd, with natural gas liquids output up 3.9 percent to 1.88 million bpd.
U.S. gasoline demand, measured by deliveries, rose 1.7 percent in May from the previous year to 8.14 million bpd.
Transportation growth drove distillate deliveries up by a strong 6 percent to 3.31 million bpd in May.
Jet fuel deliveries grew by 76,000 bpd to 1.53 million bpd, but API said the high growth rate probably reflected unusually low demand last year.
Demand for residual fuel oil was down 26,000 bpd to 800,000 bpd in May from a year ago, largely due to lower utility demand for fuel oil.
Deliveries of other oils, mainly used as petrochemical feedstocks, rose 2.7 percent to 4.6 million bpd.
